How the bias is scored
Rules-based read, not a prediction. Each timeframe gets +1/-1 per item, normalised to -1..+1: Weekly: price vs EMA10 and EMA20, EMA10 slope (vs 2 wks ago), structure (last 3 weeks vs prior 3: HH&HL +1, LH&LL -1), price above prior-week high +1 / below prior-week low -1. Daily: price vs EMA20/50/200, EMA20 slope (vs 5 days ago), structure (last 5 days vs prior 5), above PDH +1 / below PDL -1, vs prior close ±0.5. 4h (futures, 4h bars from Schwab 30-min candles, session-aligned at 18:00 ET): price vs EMA20/50, EMA20 slope (vs 3 bars ago), structure (last 4 bars vs prior 4). Overall = 0.40·Weekly + 0.35·Daily + 0.25·4h. ≥ +0.25 Bullish, ≤ −0.25 Bearish, else Neutral. Confidence: High if |score| ≥ 0.6 and all three timeframes agree in sign; Medium if |score| ≥ 0.4; else Low. Intraday context is separate: GEX regime from the 0DTE flip (above = positive gamma, damped; below = negative gamma, amplified).

How to trade gamma

Today's playbook: NQ 27,250 is 34 pts below the Flip (27,284): negative gamma. Lean toward trend and breakout trades with wider stops, and expect moves to extend. Downside magnets are the Near Put Wall 26,868 and the 1D low 27,167. A reclaim of 27,284 would flip the regime to positive.
  1. Regime first. Below the Flip = negative gamma: dealers amplify moves, so favour trend and breakout trades and use wider stops. Above the Flip = positive gamma: price tends to mean-revert, so fade the edges of the range and take quicker targets.
  2. Walls are targets and turn points. The Call Wall acts as a ceiling, the Put Wall as a floor. Price often stalls or reverses there, but if it is accepted through a wall (holds beyond it), the move often speeds up.
  3. The Flip is the line in the sand. Reclaiming it or losing it shifts the regime, and the playbook above flips with it.
  4. Trade confluence, not single lines. The best spots are where a gamma level lines up with a 1h supply/demand zone, the POC or VWAP. Even then, wait for a 1-minute trigger (Strat 2-2 or a VWAP hold) before entering.
  5. 1-day expected move (NQ 27,167 – 27,333, ±83 pts). An early tag of the min or max is stretched: look for a reversal there, don't chase.
  6. Timing. Levels matter most in the first 1–2 hours of the session and around expirations. Big news (CPI, FOMC, NFP) can override them.

Vanna & charm · QQQ

Biggest same-expiry charm sits at 27,447 (above price); charm hedging tends to pull price toward it into the close. Net charm (nearest expiry) is negative: as time passes dealers get shorter delta and buy back hedges, a drift-higher tailwind. Net vanna is positive: an IV drop (vol crush) makes dealers buy, supporting price; an IV spike makes them sell.
Net vanna (all)
$+2.30bn
per +1 IV pt

Charm target
27,447
Method

Black-Scholes vanna and charm from Schwab IV (r = 4%, no dividend), the same inputs as gamma. Dealer sign as GEX: dealers assumed long calls (+) and short puts (−). Vanna exposure = sign × OI × 100 × vanna × S × 1% = dollars of dealer delta added per +1 IV point; when IV falls 1 pt dealers trade about +vanna exposure (positive = they buy). Charm exposure = sign × OI × 100 × charm/365 × S = dollars of dealer delta added per day passing; dealers re-hedge by about −charm exposure (positive = they sell). The charm target is the strike within ±1.5% of price with the largest nearest-expiry charm, where decay-driven hedging concentrates. Flow uses Schwab totalVolume vs prior-day OI; Schwab does not report trade side.

How to trade gamma

Today's playbook: GC 4,073.9 is 57.9 above the Flip (4,016.0): positive gamma. Favour mean reversion at the range edges and quicker targets. Losing 4,016.0 flips the regime.
  1. Regime first. Below the Flip dealers amplify moves (trend, wider stops); above it price tends to mean-revert.
  2. Walls are targets and turn points. Acceptance through a wall often speeds the move up.
  3. Trade confluence, not single lines. Gamma level + POC/VWAP/supply-demand, then wait for a 1-minute trigger.
  4. Timing. Levels matter most early in the session and around expirations; big news overrides them.

Vanna & charm · SPX

Biggest same-expiry charm sits at 7,400 (below price); charm hedging tends to pull price toward it into the close. Net charm (nearest expiry) is negative: as time passes dealers get shorter delta and buy back hedges, a drift-higher tailwind. Net vanna is positive: an IV drop (vol crush) makes dealers buy, supporting price; an IV spike makes them sell.
Net vanna (all)

Charm target

Method

Black-Scholes vanna and charm from Schwab IV (r = 4%, no dividend), the same inputs as gamma. Dealer sign as GEX: dealers assumed long calls (+) and short puts (−). Vanna exposure = sign × OI × 100 × vanna × S × 1% = dollars of dealer delta added per +1 IV point; when IV falls 1 pt dealers trade about +vanna exposure (positive = they buy). Charm exposure = sign × OI × 100 × charm/365 × S = dollars of dealer delta added per day passing; dealers re-hedge by about −charm exposure (positive = they sell). The charm target is the strike within ±1.5% of price with the largest nearest-expiry charm, where decay-driven hedging concentrates. Flow uses Schwab totalVolume vs prior-day OI; Schwab does not report trade side.

Vanna & charm · SPX

Biggest same-expiry charm sits at 7,400 (below price); charm hedging tends to pull price toward it into the close. Net charm (nearest expiry) is negative: as time passes dealers get shorter delta and buy back hedges, a drift-higher tailwind. Net vanna is positive: an IV drop (vol crush) makes dealers buy, supporting price; an IV spike makes them sell.
Net vanna (all)

Charm target

Method

Black-Scholes vanna and charm from Schwab IV (r = 4%, no dividend), the same inputs as gamma. Dealer sign as GEX: dealers assumed long calls (+) and short puts (−). Vanna exposure = sign × OI × 100 × vanna × S × 1% = dollars of dealer delta added per +1 IV point; when IV falls 1 pt dealers trade about +vanna exposure (positive = they buy). Charm exposure = sign × OI × 100 × charm/365 × S = dollars of dealer delta added per day passing; dealers re-hedge by about −charm exposure (positive = they sell). The charm target is the strike within ±1.5% of price with the largest nearest-expiry charm, where decay-driven hedging concentrates. Flow uses Schwab totalVolume vs prior-day OI; Schwab does not report trade side.

Estimate, not trade-by-trade data. Built from changes in Schwab total option volume between this dashboard's own snapshots (about every 30 min while the market is open): premium = Δvolume × mark × 100, split into calls and puts. Schwab does not report who bought or sold, so a put-premium rise can be buyers or sellers. Volume is priced at the mark when the snapshot was taken, so it is approximate, and moves inside a snapshot interval are lumped at the snapshot time. Strike filter uses each snapshot's underlying price. Net is cumulative calls minus puts since the open.
